endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Require ongoing reporting to assess performance and inform decisions to scale, adjust, or sunset.

endorsements.title: FUTURE-AI: international consensus guideline for trustworthy and deployable artificial intelligence in healthcare
endorsements.quote: Implement reporting system from audits and subsequent updates | Automatic sharing of detailed reports to healthcare managers and clinicians

endorsements.title: CHAI Responsible AI Guide (Assurance Standards Guide)
endorsements.quote: Design a report that will summarize monitoring results for AI solution outputs and health system outcomes at appropriate timepoints e.g. weekly, monthly, quarterly (depending on use case).

endorsements.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework: Generative AI Profile (NIST AI 600-1)
endorsements.issuer: National Institute of Standards and Technology
endorsements.quote: Verify that AI Actors responsible for monitoring reported issues can eﬀectively evaluate GAI system performance including the application of content provenance data tracking techniques, and promptly escalate issues for response.

endorsements.title: Responsible Use of AI in Healthcare (RUAIH) guidance
endorsements.issuer: The Joint Commission and Coalition for Health AI

endorsements.title: Scaling enterprise AI in healthcare: the role of governance in risk mitigation frameworks
endorsements.quote: AI governance committees should play a central role in reviewing and monitoring AI implementations, ensuring that AI systems meet enterprise standards for safety, efficacy, and ethical considerations.

endorsements.title: AI medical device post-market surveillance regulations: consensus recommendations by the European Society of Radiology
endorsements.quote: 6 Beyond continuous monitoring, periodic reviews (e.g., every 6–12 months) of PMS data must be performed by providers and presented to deployers, to allow informed ongoing use of the medical device and facilitate timely detection of performance degradation.

endorsements.title: Equity at the point of care: auditing AI-supported resource allocation in obstetric emergencies
endorsements.quote: A minimal cadence is sufficient: a monthly MFAS dashboard huddle reviews stratified run charts by chain link and assigns owners for clusters of over-window intervals; a quarterly cross-service review reassesses target windows, routing rules, and capacity plans; and sentinel events trigger rapid reconstruction of timestamps and immediate containment actions ( 14 ).

endorsements.title: Process Improvement Before Artificial Intelligence and Automation: Building Trust With the Understand-Transform-Sustain Framework
endorsements.issuer: Mayo Clinic proceedings. Innovations, quality & outcomes
endorsements.quote: On a larger scale, a multidisciplinary team could periodically review dashboards and scorecards to measure the efficacy of the deployed tool.

endorsements.title: A testable framework linking diagnostic AI contribution to outcome measurement in clinical decision support
endorsements.quote: Metrics should be integrated into monitoring dashboards, quality-improvement cycles, clinical governance committees, patient-safety processes, and de-implementation procedures.

commentary.bottom_line: Nine sources, including CHAI, NIST, FUTURE-AI, and the European Society of Radiology, endorse scheduled governance review of monitoring reports and dashboards, but no supplied study tests the practice or documents the hazard it targets. Adoption would rest on expert consensus alone.

perspectives.view: No supplied study tests whether scheduled committee review of monitoring reports changes decisions or patient outcomes, and no study documents how often monitoring data go unused. The nine endorsements come from frameworks, guidance, and commentaries. Under GRADE conventions, consensus statements do not count as evidence of effect, so certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence.

The European Society of Radiology recommends periodic review of post-market surveillance data every 6 to 12 months, presented to deployers. NIST AI 600-1 asks that monitoring staff be able to escalate issues promptly. These sources describe expected oversight practice, but none reports whether such review met regulatory aims in any tested setting.

The endorsements propose cadences that range from weekly or monthly dashboard huddles to quarterly cross-service reviews and reviews every 6 to 12 months. No supplied study reports the staff time, cost, or committee capacity required, so a health system cannot yet estimate the resources needed to sustain this practice across many deployed tools.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that compare health systems with and without scheduled governance review of AI monitoring data and that measure the time from a detected performance problem to a logged corrective action, the share of flagged issues that receive a response, and downstream patient outcomes. Research should also examine which review cadence fits which type of tool and what committee staffing the practice requires.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. One commentary on obstetric resource allocation proposes monthly review of stratified run charts, which suggests dashboards could be built to show subgroup differences, but whether governance review of such data reduces disparities has not been tested.
